answer_bank.title: Automated a weekly reporting pipeline
answer_bank.situation: The analytics team hand-built a weekly KPI report in spreadsheets — about a day of copy-paste every Monday and frequent transcription errors.
answer_bank.task: I offered to remove the manual step entirely and make the numbers reproducible and auditable.
answer_bank.action: Wrote a small Python pipeline that pulled from the warehouse, validated each metric against the previous run, rendered a report, and posted it to the shared drive with a run id and a log.
answer_bank.result: Cut the Monday task from ~6 hours to under 5 minutes, removed the class of transcription errors, and the team adopted the run-id trail for audits.

answer_bank.title: Built an evaluation harness for a RAG assistant
answer_bank.situation: A support-docs RAG assistant kept 'improving' in demos while nobody could say whether retrieval had actually regressed between changes.
answer_bank.task: Make answer quality measurable so a change could be accepted or rejected on evidence.
answer_bank.action: Assembled a labelled question set with known-good passages, scored retrieval (recall@k) and answer faithfulness on every change, and gated merges on the numbers rather than on a demo.
answer_bank.result: Two 'obvious' prompt tweaks turned out to lower faithfulness and were reverted; the harness became the definition of done for the assistant.

answer_bank.title: Cut a model endpoint's tail latency
answer_bank.situation: An internal inference endpoint met its median SLA but blew past it at p95, which is what users actually felt.
answer_bank.task: Bring p95 under budget without buying a bigger machine.
answer_bank.action: Profiled the request path, found the cost was a cold prefix re-encoded on every call, cached it, and moved a language-conditional block to the end of the prompt so the cache held.
answer_bank.result: p95 dropped by roughly half and the median barely moved — the fix was about variance, not raw throughput.

answer_bank.title: Disagreed with a launch decision, on evidence
answer_bank.situation: A team wanted to ship an LLM feature that looked great on cherry-picked examples but had no offline evaluation behind it.
answer_bank.task: Raise the risk without simply blocking the team.
answer_bank.action: Ran a quick labelled sample, showed where it failed on realistic inputs, and proposed a one-week eval-gate before launch rather than a veto.
answer_bank.result: The team took the week, found and fixed a whole failure class, and shipped with a metric they could defend.

answer_bank.title: Picked up a new framework under a deadline
answer_bank.situation: A project needed a streaming websocket UI in a stack I had not used before, with a fixed demo date.
answer_bank.task: Get to a working, honest demo without faking it.
answer_bank.action: Built the smallest end-to-end slice first, read the framework's own examples rather than blog posts, and kept a list of what I did not yet understand so I would not overclaim it later.
answer_bank.result: The demo worked on real data, and I could say precisely which parts were solid and which were prototype.

answer_bank.title: Onboarded a junior engineer onto the codebase
answer_bank.situation: A new hire was stuck for days on a pipeline whose failure modes were all tribal knowledge.
answer_bank.task: Get them productive and stop the knowledge living only in my head.
answer_bank.action: Paired on their first real fix, then wrote the gotchas down as short runbooks so the next person would not need me.
answer_bank.result: They shipped independently within the week, and the runbooks cut the same questions from later hires.
